$comment: One description per model: how to reach it, and what it costs.
The API key never lives here -- it stays in the env file. This file is
safe to commit and to publish beside a score, which is the point: a
benchmark number is meaningless without the price basis it was computed
Prices are USD per million tokens. 'cached_input_usd_per_mtok' is the
discounted rate for the cached SHARE of input, not an extra charge on
top -- the exporter splits the input total, it does not add to it. Null
means the provider publishes no cached rate, and the exporter then bills
cached tokens at the full input rate rather than inventing a discount.
A null price yields a null cost column, never a zero and never a guess.
Costs are computed at export time, so correcting a price here and
re-exporting fixes every trial already on disk retroactively.

minimax/MiniMax-M3.pricing_source: https://api.minimax.io direct-API rates (not OpenRouter's reseller rates of 0.23/0.96/0.05)
pricing_notes: Direct MiniMax API rates, matching the endpoint in bench.env. A reseller
such as OpenRouter charges differently, so switching endpoint means
Cache WRITES are free; only cache reads are metered, which is what
cached_input_usd_per_mtok bills. cached_prompt_tokens is the share OF
input, so the exporter splits the input total rather than adding to it.
Requests over 512K input tokens bill the WHOLE request at 2x every rate.
Not modelled: the largest prompt observed on this suite is ~21K tokens,
two orders of magnitude below the threshold. Revisit if a task ever
approaches it -- trials/input_tokens_largest_call is the column to watch.
